title: AI Photo Restoration
summary: Free AI photo restoration: remove scratches, mend tears, fix faded colour, sharpen blurry faces and colorize black and white prints. See 5 before and afters.
body_markdown:
### Is there a free AI photo restoration tool?


Yes. Flick is free to start: the free plan gives 100 credits every day with no credit card, and GPT Image 2.6, which restored every photo on this page, costs 5 credits an edit.


### How do I restore an old photo with AI?


Scan or photograph the print, add it to an image edit model, and write a prompt that names each kind of damage to remove and lists the people, clothes and framing that must stay exactly the same.


### Can AI fix a torn or ripped photo?


Yes. Scan every piece in place, then ask the model to close the tear and fill any missing area by continuing what is already in the picture, such as a wall, a roof or the sky, without inventing new people or objects.


### Can AI colorize a black and white photo?


Yes. Describe the colour of the hair, eyes, clothes and background and ask the model to keep everything else the same; the colours it picks are a plausible guess, so name any you know from family memory.


### Can AI fix a blurry old photo?


Yes, within limits. A restore prompt can bring a soft or shaken photo into focus, but the sharp detail it adds is redrawn rather than recovered, so check each face against the original.


### Does AI photo restoration change faces?


It can. The model redraws what it repairs, so small or damaged faces may come back slightly different; asking it to keep the same faces and comparing a few versions with the original gives the closest likeness.


### Can I animate a restored photo?


Yes. Use the restored photo as the start frame of an image to video model in Flick and describe one small movement, such as a blink or a smile, and ask it to keep the look of the photograph.
